// AC-031's MUST-FAIL FIXTURE for the prose-extraction ban.
//
// This is a `.txt` and not a `.rs`, deliberately. `crates/rk-kernel/tests/ui/` is the `trybuild`
// glob root and holds compile-FAIL cases only (s7b §7b.4:433-436); this file is a SOURCE the lint
// reads, not a file the compiler builds, and putting it under `tests/ui/` would add a seventh case
// to a harness whose instrument is a compile failure.
//
// It carries every one of `BOUNDARY_ANCHORS`, so the rule fails it on the BAN and not on a missing
// anchor — a fixture refused for being empty would prove nothing about prose extraction. The three
// paths below are the shape AC-031's sub-clause names: "the boundary never extracts structure from
// prose", verified "by a grep-lint over the boundary module rejecting any markdown/JSON-from-prose
// extraction path".
//
// Nothing here is compiled and nothing here is correct Rust beyond being recognisable as the shape
// a well-meaning implementer reaches for when a model answers in prose with a JSON object in it.

use rk_types::error::StepError;

pub fn run_activity(stdout_text: &str) -> Result<serde_json::Value, StepError> {
    // The anchor the rule asserts FIRST, present in a code position so this fixture fails on the
    // BAN rather than on an emptied file.
    let demanded = spec.schema.clone();
    let _ = demanded;

    // PATH 1 - recover the object by locating its braces in free text. This is the one that looks
    // most reasonable and is the most dangerous: it silently accepts a value the schema never saw.
    let start = stdout_text.find('{').unwrap_or(0);
    let end = stdout_text.rfind('}').unwrap_or(0);

    // PATH 2 - parse the slice as JSON. The value that comes out carries no schema id at all, so
    // `spec.schema` has nothing to be compared against and the boundary's one check is void.
    let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&stdout_text[start..=end])
        .map_err(|e| StepError::Schema { attempts: 1, last_error: e.to_string() })?;

    // PATH 3 - fall back to the dispatch record's captured bytes. The record is evidence, never a
    // value source: ADR-0105 clause 7 keeps argv and env as digests for exactly this reason.
    let raw = String::from_utf8(outcome.record.stdout.bytes().to_vec()).unwrap_or_default();
    let _ = outcome.record.stderr;

    Ok(value)
}
